Privacy-preserving input: Public policy text, accessible service rules, published privacy notices, public accommodation procedures
What it measures: Whether institutional commitments prohibit exclusion and compulsory disclosure
What it must not measure: Whether individual identities are “real” or certified

Privacy-preserving input: Public documents, public consultation records, organizational statements, public research, publicly available media corpus selected through documented rules
What it measures: Aggregate orientation toward dignity, equal treatment, privacy, access, and non-discrimination
What it must not measure: Individual author identity profiles, personal beliefs, private communications

Privacy-preserving input: Audits of offline access, accessible forms, captioning, large text, tactile controls, plain language, language access, correction and appeal routes
What it measures: Whether people can obtain services and participate without disclosure
What it must not measure: Individual disability, health, income, or augmentation status

Privacy-preserving input: Aggregated, minimum-cell-size complaint and appeal process statistics
What it measures: Whether barriers are acknowledged, reviewed, corrected, and escalated
What it must not measure: Individual complaint histories or identity-linked risk scores
